### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/publish-and-preview.mdx`  _(via PLUGIN_MANIFEST_INVALID (literal, a string literal in handleInstall))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `be35afd0af6e109323f83d983e102e77583789dd` — the merge of head `efb9823b3259644e4ccc198fc861da5a1f5e084f` into base `951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin be35afd0af6e109323f83d983e102e77583789dd && git checkout be35afd0af6e109323f83d983e102e77583789dd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f efb9823b3259644e4ccc198fc861da5a1f5e084f && git checkout -B drift-repro 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f && git merge --no-ff efb9823b3259644e4ccc198fc861da5a1f5e084f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fd6638db1598cf82c70c3cb2afdb4ec3117bdffe`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-namespace-gate-33922.test.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts, packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts, packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, content/docs/deployment/publish-and-preview.mdx, skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md (all read at the head, none in the diff, none reviewed)

**FAIL on one must-fix (F1).** The narrowing itself is sound: it makes the spec's own refusal real and takes no declared capability away. But the new gate does not read the key the registry installs under for every body shape this door accepts, so the claim "no later step ever sees a namespace no author can declare" does not yet hold. F1 is derived by reading the head; nothing was run, so it is not measured.

Inputs read: card #33922 body and its 3 comments (triage 6895918518, claim 6906172715, dev report 6908560000), the PR body, the net diff of 3 files against `22bcc7699c`, and the 51 check-runs on the head. No check-run failed: 35 succeeded and 16 were skipped.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, inline manifest: right.** A `namespace` that `ManifestSchema.shape.namespace` refuses (`''`, `QA_N`, `9-Bad Ns!`, a non-string) moves from `200` to `400 PLUGIN_MANIFEST_INVALID`. The gate sits right after the id gate, where the inline and cloud branches have converged, and ahead of every write.
- **Accept-set, cloud snapshot and grant path: right.** The same values answer `502`, the status this door already gives an invalid upstream snapshot. `installForGrant` goes through `handleInstall`, so it is covered.
- **Absent namespace: right.** The declaration is `.optional()`, and `undefined` parses.
- **`namespace: null`: right, but unnamed.** `z.string().optional()` refuses `null`, so a body that wrote `null` moves from installed-as-no-namespace to `400`. The changeset describes only string values (nit N2).
- **Artifact members: right to leave alone.** `resolveArtifactPackageEntries` parses each `packages[]` entry whole through `ArtifactPackageSchema` and throws `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGE_ENTRY` / 422. A second judge would move that answer.
- **Rehydrate and the `:manifestId` routes: right to leave ungated.** Rehydrate registers ledger entries directly and never enters `handleInstall`, so an entry an older build wrote still loads and can be removed.
- **Unmanaged copy and customization pair: right.** Both run inside `handleInstall` after the gate. A pair's namespace is `BASE_custom`, which the spec holds to the same grammar (`customization-package.ts`), so no conforming pair is refused.
- **Public surface: unchanged.** No export, schema key, error code or route is added or re-shaped. The code is the existing `PLUGIN_MANIFEST_INVALID`; the sentence is the declaration's own inside the frame `judgeInstallMode` already uses.
- **Where the gate reads the namespace: wrong for one shape.** See F1.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

- `@objectstack/cloud-connection` at `patch` with the `!` title and a `**BREAKING**` block is the level the narrowing arm owes. The `Check Changeset` check-run succeeded on this head.
- `Clause-②:` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear on both the PR body and the changeset, and they agree. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: nothing an author can write through the declaration moved.
- **BREAKING text: accurate, with one gap.** The FROM/TO pair for the inline manifest and for the snapshot match the code. The "Not moved" list matches what I read (absent namespace, artifact member, conforming namespace, registry gate, rehydrate and uninstall of an older entry). The gap is `null` (N2). The sentence that `QA_N` "installed beside an existing owner of `qa_n`" matches the card's reproduction and the dev's ablation.
- **ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: holds.** No schema key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped. No stored row, ledger entry or authored value is rewritten, and rehydrate is ungated, so there is nothing for a conversion to rewrite and no tombstone to leave. The one stranded case (an entry an older build installed under a refused namespace cannot be re-installed) is stated in the changeset with its remedy, and it concerns only values no build tool could have produced.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report carries `open_questions: []`, 7 deviations and 2 out-of-scope notes.

- **Deviations 1 to 4** (repo-wide lint, dependents' suites and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` left to CI; main merged once): answered by the head's check-runs. `Lint · ESLint`, all 8 `Test Core` shards, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` succeeded on `fd6638db`, which is itself a merge of main.
- **Deviation 5** (commit trailers): not a contract matter; the PR-body guards check-run succeeded.
- **Deviation 6** (no second judge for artifact members): accepted, see ①.
- **Deviation 7** (the `installModes` frame around the declaration's sentence): accepted. The namespace declaration's sentence names neither the key nor the value, so a frame is needed, and this one is the door's own.
- **Out-of-scope note 1** (an artifact member's refusal leaves as a thrown 422; its HTTP envelope was not measured): unchanged by this diff. Not a finding here; it can ride a follow-up card if the seat wants the envelope pinned.
- **Out-of-scope note 2, and the area's point 2: `POST /api/v1/packages` does parse the namespace.** The door parses the WHOLE body through `PackageInstallBodySchema` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, the `declaredBody` verdict). Both branches of that union bind `PackageInstallManifestSchema`, which is `ManifestSchema.extend(...)` and so carries the namespace grammar. A failed parse answers `400` before either install limb, and every later read goes through the parsed value. `packages-install-body-contract.test.ts` pins `manifest.namespace` outside the grammar (`Acme-CRM`). So a namespace this door now refuses cannot be installed through that one. For the declaration this means the narrowing is not undone by a sibling door: with this PR, `defineStack`, `os build`, the artifact-entry parse, `POST /api/v1/packages` and install-local all refuse the same values. No finding and no follow-up card is owed for it.
- **The area's point 1: `content/docs/deployment/publish-and-preview.mdx` is still true, but now incomplete.** Its paragraph says a collision is the second refusal, that the install parses `manifest.id` first, and that a bad id answers `400 PLUGIN_MANIFEST_INVALID` (`502` from a catalog snapshot). Every sentence still holds. What it no longer does is list every cause of that code at this door: a refused `namespace` now answers it too, also ahead of the collision check. See N1 for what the `Skills-docs:` line owes.
- **Escalated: none.** F1's mechanism went to the seat, not here.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real.** `ManifestSchema.shape.namespace` on `main` is `z.string().regex(NAMESPACE_PATTERN, ...).optional()`, with `NAMESPACE_PATTERN = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,19}$/`. The spec declares no value that this door now refuses: the reserved `base`, `system` and `sys` conform, a customization pair's `BASE_custom` is held to the same grammar, and absence stays admitted. The gate references the declaration and copies no grammar, so a future move of the rule reaches this door with no edit. This is enforcement of a declared refusal, not a capability narrowed at the consumer.

I tried to break it four ways. Three held: a sibling door (closed, see ③), a legitimate namespace the grammar would strand (none found), and an earlier write before the gate (none; only the cloud fetch precedes it). One did not hold.

**F1 — must-fix. The gate must judge the key the registry installs under.** The new leg and the registry each read the namespace off the body, and they do not read it the same way. For the shapes the tests pin, those are the same key. For one accepted body shape they are not, and by reading the head the gate then admits a body whose registered namespace the declaration refuses, which is the card's defect. The diff's own docblock says the leg reads "the key ... the registry's install-time namespace gate compare[s]"; for that shape this is not so.
  - Rule-level fix: at step 1b″, parse the namespace at the key registration reads. Add a pin for the shape, with its ablation.
  - This is derived by reading the head and is not measured. The dev measures it first. If a later step is shown to refuse that shape before the register, the finding falls to pinning that refusal.
  - The mechanism and the shape went to the seat, not to GitHub.
  - It is a finding on this PR, because the read site is chosen by this diff. The two older legs that read through the same helper (the install-mode judge and the writable-holder check) are not in the diff; they earn a follow-up card, worded at rule level.

**N1 — nit, prose face (PR body). The `Skills-docs:` line answers for `skills/**` and is silent on `content/docs/**`.** A `(narrowing)` arm owes the PR body a `Skills-docs:` line; the changeset does not owe one, so its absence there is not a defect. The line is present and its skills half is true: `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` teaches `manifest.namespace` as optional but enforced once set. But `none` leaves out the one page the drift bot named, which enumerates this door's pre-collision refusals and does not yet name the namespace. The repo's own precedent for a page that lists causes and lacks the new one is `follow-up owed — FILES`. The line should read `follow-up owed — content/docs/deployment/publish-and-preview.mdx`, and the seat rewrites it to the card number before ACCEPT. No head move.

**N2 — nit, prose face (changeset). The BREAKING block does not name `null` or a non-string.** A manifest that wrote `namespace: null` installed before as a package with no namespace and now answers `400`. "A manifest with no `namespace` installs as before" is true only of an absent key. One clause in the changeset fixes it. No build tool emits that value, so nothing else follows from it.

**N3 — nit, accepted deviation. No pin for `null` or for a too-long or one-character namespace.** The declaration is referenced, so these follow from the schema; the test pins four refused values and that is enough for the contract.

Delta review: F1's fix moves the head and earns one. N1 and N2 are fixed on the prose faces and need none.

## Review — FAIL (one must-fix, from the contract record)

Head-sha: `fd6638db1598cf82c70c3cb2afdb4ec3117bdffe`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-16T06:26Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `22bcc769` (3 files, +395/−0, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5 (area S3 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM; the contract face by an isolated sub-agent at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

**Contract face:** a declared narrowing, so the whole diff is under the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record posted beside this comment (FAIL, `Local-runs: none`). This ACCEPT read adopts its findings.

**Must-fix (blocks landing)**

1. **F1: the namespace gate must judge the same key the registry installs under.** For one body shape this door accepts, the new leg reads the namespace from a different place than registration reads it, so a namespace the declaration refuses can still be registered. That is the card's defect, still reachable on that shape. The diff's own docblock says the leg reads the key the registry's gate compares, and for that shape it does not. This is derived by reading the head, not measured. The mechanism went to the seat, not to GitHub. Fix it at rule level: parse the namespace at the key registration reads, and pin that shape with an ablation. Measure first: if a later step is shown to refuse the shape before the register, the finding falls to pinning that refusal. Either way the head moves and earns a delta review.

**What holds**

- The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real. `ManifestSchema.shape.namespace` is used by reference, absence stays admitted, and `base`, `system`, `sys` and a pair's `BASE_custom` all conform.
- The gate sits right after the id gate and ahead of every write, with the same 400 (caller) / 502 (upstream) split and the same rehydrate and `:manifestId` exemption. The pins cover four refused values, a non-string, a compiled bundle, the snapshot's 502, absent and conforming controls, the unmoved artifact-member refusal, and `QA_N` beside `qa_n` over a real engine.
- `POST /api/v1/packages` already parses the namespace through `PackageInstallBodySchema` (`ManifestSchema.extend`) and pins it, so no sibling door undoes the narrowing. No card is owed for it.
- `patch` with `!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are all right.

**Nits (prose faces; no re-review of their own)**

- **N1.** The PR body's `Skills-docs:` line should read `follow-up owed — content/docs/deployment/publish-and-preview.mdx`. That page lists this door's pre-collision refusals and does not yet name the namespace. The seat rewrites the line to the card number before ACCEPT.
- **N2.** The changeset's BREAKING block should name `namespace: null`. It installed before as no namespace and now answers 400. "A manifest with no `namespace` installs as before" is true only of an absent key.
- **N3.** There is no pin for `null`, a one-character or an over-long value. This is accepted, because the declaration is referenced.

**Follow-up (for the seat):** two older legs of this door read the namespace or `installModes` through the same helper, and they want a card worded at rule level. Details went to the seat.

**Gates:** at review time 35 success, 16 skipped, none red.
